labels.label: bprop:project

hypotheses.paper: f : S -> M an isometric immersion of a complete Riemannian hypersurface; S~, D o f~
hypotheses.note: any connected T2 space X with F : X -> Mn a SpacelikeDevelopment (local embedding onto spacelike Lipschitz pieces) whose pulled-back length is complete; the compatibility of the pulled-length topology with X's topology is derived (SpacelikeDevelopment.continuous_toSpace), not assumed; simple connectivity of X is not used

hypotheses.paper: Q(Delta) = Mn/Delta with the metric making pi isometric on Delta-orthogonal hyperplanes
hypotheses.note: Q(Delta) modelled TOPOLOGICALLY by the hyperplane Delta-perp (orthSub), pi = projection along Delta, the identity on Delta-perp. The paper's metric is minkQ restricted to Delta-perp (positive definite); the subtype carries the sup-product metric of R x R^d, equivalent but not equal. Only the topology enters the homeomorphism.

findings: W5 confirmed, l.2244-2257: the maximal lifting c of an arbitrary path c-bar is Cauchy only if c-bar is rectifiable (the bound d(c(t_n), c(t_m)) <= length of c-bar on [t_n, t_m]). Repair: lift straight segments only. The step 'distance increasing, and thus, a local homeomorphism' (l.2244-2245) is NOT a defect of the paper: in Barbot's smooth setting the differential of pi o D o f~ satisfies |d pi(v)| >= |v| on spacelike v, so it is an immersion between manifolds of equal dimension (n-1) and a local diffeomorphism by the inverse function theorem (or, read metrically, local injectivity plus invariance of domain); the step is a standard implicit one. Only in this campaign's Lipschitz generalisation (no differential) must it be argued otherwise: from the local graph structure (pi injective on the c<1 pieces) plus an intermediate-value argument along Delta-lines, as planned in isCoveringMap_projAlong_comp's comment.

Closer round 2 (2026-11-01): PROVED with no sorry (#print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The route differs from the obstruction's step (iv): instead of assembling evenly covered sheets, the radial lift of straight segments from one base point is shown to be a continuous section (a clopen argument along [0,1] of the parameter, isHomeomorph_of_lift_segment), and a continuous section of a local homeomorphism of a connected Hausdorff space through one point of a fibre is a two-sided inverse; the covering then follows from the homeomorphism (isCoveringMap_of_isHomeomorph). The paper's order (covering, then simply connected) is inverted, which is legitimate because the target Q(Delta) is a normed space (star-shaped). The step (ii) TOPOLOGY, which 8.1 does not assume, is proved for every spacelike development of a Hausdorff X (SpacelikeDevelopment.continuous_toSpace, first exit from a compact frame cylinder pulled back through the embedding F|U); the length bound (iii) is exact: minkQ v <= minkQ (pi v) for timelike Delta (minkQ_eq_projAlong).
labels.notes: Non-vacuity (kb/0011, audit minor 4, applied): spacelikeDevelopment_slice + completeSpace_pulledLength_slice inhabit the hypotheses of 8.1 and 8.3 (X = R^d connected T2, F = the slice t = 0, pulled length isometric to R^d). Marked: bprop_project is sorry-free and its hypotheses are only weakened (any connected T2 X, Lipschitz spacelike development, complete pulled length, in the DEC-35 reading of the metric notion); the master may unmark if the [2.4] reading question is held to bear on 8.1.

labels.label: [8.G] the graph remark, and bcor:quo's last clause

hypotheses.note: proved from bprop_project with no further sorry; now sorry-free (#print axioms isEntireAcausalGraph_range: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound)

findings: l.2307-2309 'the graph of a contracting map' is proved in the strict form (IsEntireAcausalGraph: acausal, i.e. strictly contracting, and meeting every timelike line). Strictness is not automatic from 8.1: 8.1 for every timelike Delta only gives a 1-Lipschitz graph; a 1-Lipschitz graph attaining slope 1 between two points contains the whole null segment (lipschitzWith_one_segment), which a point-locally c<1 piece cannot contain (IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.not_eventually_add_smul_mem). The paper does not say why the contraction is strict.

findings: W6 confirmed, l.2287-2290: 'completely similar' hides two distinct steps, an openness step by the intermediate value theorem (no completeness) and a closedness step that is the completeness argument of 8.1 run on the (n-2)-dimensional S~ cap P0; the projection P0 -> P0/Delta0 restricted to S~ cap P0 is indeed isometric (Delta0 is the null direction of P0).

Closer round 2 (2026-11-01): PROVED with no sorry (#print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), and without the open/closed split of the previous obstruction: normalise Delta0 = l.1 (1, e) with |e| = 1, project along (1, e) onto R^d (nullProj e : w -> w.2 - w.1 e, kernel R(1, e), a local homeomorphism on F by the same intermediate value argument as 8.1, now for a causal direction; exists_chart_of_proj), and lift the segment from Psi(F x0) to Psi(r) with direction v orthogonal to e, i.e. inside one level of P0, where minkQ of the developed velocity is exactly the squared Euclidean speed (minkQ_eq_nullProj: minkQ w = |Psi w|^2 + 2 w.1 <Psi w, e>). This is Barbot's 'completely similar ... the projection onto P0/Delta0 is an isometry on S cap P0' made literal: the lifting machinery of 8.1 is reused unchanged. Neither 8.1 nor ConnectedSpace X is used (ConnectedSpace X stays in the statement).

findings: Against the design (BARBOT-WAVE3.md §4, 'External: the homeomorphism half of 8.11 ... not used below'): (CC')'s DevelopsCC is stated on S^ = p^-1(S) in the universal cover of M, whereas Barbot's §8 works on the universal cover S~ of S with a lift f~ (l.2215-2223). They agree iff S^ is connected, i.e. pi1(S) -> pi1(M) is onto, which Barbot never states and which, for a Cauchy surface, is the topological splitting (Prop 8.11, class E). So the bridge as stated against p^-1(S) depends on 8.11's homeomorphism half (B1), or on an independent retraction argument. Stating DevelopsCC on S~ (a covering of S, with f~) would avoid it for 8.1/8.3 but move it to the injectivity of D on p^-1(S) used by 8.12.

kb_proposals: Gluing chart-local lengths needs no subdivision: take the density at t in the chart AT c t (localDensity φ c t, φ x = chart at x); locality and Isom-invariance become one pointwise lemma (localDensity_chartSys_eq), and the pseudo-emetric laws are proved once for any 'local developing system' φ : X → X → 𝐌ⁿ (charts, or a single developing map).

A covering of a simply connected, locally path-connected space by a connected space is a homeomorphism in ten lines: lift the identity (IsCoveringMap.existsUnique_continuousMap_lifts), then IsCoveringMap.eq_of_comp_eq (isHomeomorph_of_isCoveringMap).

A Submodule of 𝐌ⁿ used as a type is SimplyConnectedSpace and LocPathConnectedSpace by inferInstance (RealTopologicalVectorSpace.contractibleSpace, LocallyConvexSpace): model a quotient 𝐌ⁿ/Δ by Δ^⊥ rather than by the quotient module.

Local-to-global Lipschitz along a path: IsLocLip of γ.extend gives a global Lipschitz bound via LocallyLipschitzOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_compact on Icc 0 1, then γ.extend = γ.extend ∘ projIcc and LipschitzWith.projIcc (isLocLip_pulled_iff).

Never `set` a term occurring in the TYPE of a bound variable before a `change`: `set` re-introduces the variable and the goal then mentions the shadowed x✝, so `change` fails; state the lemma on the base type instead.

Completeness lifts along a covering without a path-lifting library: take mathlib's IsEvenlyCovered data (U, H : f⁻¹U ≃ₜ U × fibre) at the limit; the sheet index t ↦ (H (γ t)).2 is constant along any path in f⁻¹U (PreconnectedSpace.constant, fibre discrete), and t ↦ H.symm (β t, i) lifts a path of U on sheet i (completeSpace_pulledLength_restrict).

A path is at least as long as the distance to any of its points: reparametrise by s ↦ γ.extend (t·s); its extend is γ.extend ∘ (t · projIcc), 1-Lipschitz, so LocLipAt transfers (LocLipAt.comp_lipschitz) and the length is localLength over [0, t] (LocalLengthSpace.edist_le_pathLength).

A homeomorphism S × ℝ ≃ₜ Y with ψ(x,0) = x makes p⁻¹(S) connected in the ported UniversalCover: retract a path α⁻¹·β rel endpoints into S and lift it with UniversalCover.liftFrom, whose endpoint class is built in (connectedSpace_preimage_of_splitting).
In a file with `open scoped unitInterval`, `σ` is notation (unitInterval.symm): a local `let σ := …` fails with 'Invalid pattern variable'.

Segment lifting without covering theory: for a local homeomorphism q of a Hausdorff space onto a normed space, exists_lift_segment_of_mapClusterPt (sup of the lift times, the glued lift on [0, T*), a cluster point at T*, extension through a chart: exists_lift_glue) and isHomeomorph_of_lift_segment (the radial lift is continuous by a clopen argument on [0,1] of the parameter; a continuous section through one point is an inverse on a connected space). Covering then comes free from the homeomorphism (isCoveringMap_of_isHomeomorph, fibre PUnit through IsEvenlyCovered.to_isEvenlyCovered_preimage).

Projecting along a null direction: for |e| = 1, nullProj e w = w.2 - w.1 e has kernel R(1, e), and minkQ w = |nullProj e w|^2 + 2 w.1 <nullProj e w, e>; on the level <., e> = const (a null hyperplane) minkQ is the squared Euclidean norm of the projection (minkQ_eq_nullProj, minkB_nullProj).

The IVT openness of a projection of a spacelike Lipschitz piece holds for any causal Delta != 0 (IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.eventually_exists_add_smul_mem): in the c<1 frame, c |Delta'.2| <= c |Delta'.1| < |Delta'.1| needs only Delta'.1 != 0.
